html:
The Western Desert language, also called Wati, is a chain of closely related Aboriginal dialects spoken across the deserts of Western Australia, South Australia and the Northern Territory. It belongs to the Pama-Nyungan family and covers more land than any other Aboriginal language.

Neighbouring dialects are easily understood, distant ones less so. The best known include Pitjantjatjara, Pintupi and Kukatja; groups such as the Tjalkadjara, Nyanganyatjara, Ngaatjatjarra and Yulparija spoke forms of it.

One language over so much desert reflects the way of life there: small bands moving far between waterholes, linked by marriage, trade, law and song lines. Several dialects are still learned by children, which is rare among Aboriginal languages. See Desert hunter-gatherers.
